SUMMARY 
Pace Scheduler is a cloud‑based workforce management system designed for law enforcement, giving Probation staff 24/7 access on any device while streamlining scheduling through permanent shifts, rotation patterns, automated deficit tracking, open‑shift sign‑ups, electronic time‑off and overtime requests, mass communication tools, and detailed audit‑ready reporting. Alongside it, the integrated Timeclock Module replaces the current manual, inconsistent timekeeping processes at Juvenile Institutions by allowing staff to clock in and out electronically, automatically linking timestamps to scheduled shifts, reducing discrepancies, improving real‑time attendance oversight, and generating accurate payroll data-all within the same unified platform.
 
DISCUSSION:
Probation Juvenile Institutions currently rely on a paper master schedule system for staffing. The paper system requires administrators to find a physical copy of the master shift report to calculate and report staffing patterns. A paper system can lead to inaccuracies and inefficiencies. This program is needed to modernize antiquated paper processes by introducing centralized, digital scheduling and workforce management. By automating shift assignments, documenting staffing levels in real time, and maintaining a comprehensive audit trail, the system ensures accurate reporting and immediate visibility into staffing compliance.
 
The Pace Scheduler software is an advanced scheduling solution built specifically for the unique needs of law enforcement. It is an online-hosted solution, which allows users 24-7 access anywhere they have an active internet connection. The site is scalable and fully functional on any modern device (tablet, phone, laptop, PC, etc.).  It will allow Probation to quickly and easily create schedules utilizing permanent shift and customized rotation patterns, easily identify and fill staffing deficits, manage on-the-fly schedule changes, notify and allow officers sign up for available open-shifts, send unlimited communication via email and/or text alerts and messages to staff, handle time off/overtime requests electronically, all backed by a full audit trail and extremely robust reporting, and ease the burden on administrative staff by automating the process. 
 
In addition to the scheduling platform, Probation is procuring the Pace Scheduler Timeclock Module to further modernize workforce management across both Juvenile Institutions. Currently, staff timekeeping is managed through disparate, manual processes that are susceptible to human error, inconsistency, and administrative inefficiency. The integration of a unified timeclock solution directly within the Pace Scheduler platform will standardize time and attendance tracking across both institutions, ensuring that all staff operate under a single, cohesive system. The Timeclock Module allows employees to clock in and out electronically, with timestamps automatically recorded and linked to their assigned shifts in the master schedule. This eliminates discrepancies between scheduled and actual hours worked, provides supervisors with real-time attendance visibility, and generates accurate data for payroll processing-all within the same platform already being used for scheduling.
The adoption of the Timeclock Module supports the Department’s broader goal of operational standardization and procedural consistency. By consolidating scheduling and timekeeping into one integrated platform, Probation will reduce the administrative burden associated with reconciling records from multiple systems, minimize opportunities for error, and establish uniform operating procedures that apply equally to staff at both facilities. The module’s audit trail capabilities further ensure accountability and transparency in time reporting, which is critical for compliance with labor regulations and internal policy requirements. This investment represents a strategic step toward a fully integrated, data-driven approach to workforce management that will serve both institutions equitably and efficiently for years to come.
 
The non-standard agreement terms include limitations of liability and proprietary rights. The Chief Probation Officer recommends approval of this proposed Agreement.

The funds for this Agreement are included in the Probation Department (PRO001, Unit 8163 and PRO001, Unit 8164) Fiscal Year (FY) 2025-26 Adopted Budget. SUMMARY:
The Pajaro Sunny Mesa Springfield Area Regional Consolidation Project would combine the following public water systems and private wells into one regional public water system to be operated by the Pajaro Sunny Mesa Community Services District (PSMCSD):
·	Pajaro water system (PWS; 463 active connections, consisting of 358 residential connections and 105 commercial/industrial connections);
·	Sunny Mesa water system (SMWS; 268 active connections, consisting of 257 residential connections and 11 commercial connections); 
·	Springfield water system (SWS; 159 residential connections and two commercial/industrial connections)
·	Two state-regulated water systems, nine small water systems, and private wells north of Moss Landing (NOML; 77 connections, consisting of 34 residential connections on water systems and 43 residential connections on private domestic wells).

The Proposed Project is necessary to address long-standing contamination and vulnerability within the PWS, SMWS, SWS, and NOML systems. The Proposed Project area consists of the existing and proposed future service areas of the PWS, the SMWS, the SWS, and the NOML area. Additionally, the regional public water system’s service area would be expanded to include eight parcels that are not currently within the PSMCSD’s service area. Once fully operational, the proposed project would serve approximately 967 total connections. See Exhibits I and J.

PSMCSD prepared an Initial Study and adopted a Mitigated Negative Declaration (MND) for the project. Mitigation measures were adopted for potential biological resources, cultural resources, hazards and hazardous materials, hydrology and water quality, noise, tribal cultural resources, and utilities and service systems. Much of the service area is rural and/or agricultural and this project was found to have less than significant growth-inducing impacts. Mitigation measures that are needed to demonstrate compliance with County Code have been applied as conditions of approval to this permit. 

This project will provide a reliable source of potable water to PSMCSD customers. Consolidating the Pajaro Sunny Mesa Springfield Area systems and mitigating for impacts to resources, the project is consistent with the North County Area Plan, North County Land Use Plan, and Coastal Implementation Plan policies.   

DISCUSSION:
The project would primarily be supplied with water from three sources, comprised of Pajaro Wells Nos. 1 and 2, and Springfield Well No. 2. The two Pajaro Wells would operate on alternating days to meet the average daily demand for the consolidated water system. Additionally, SMWS Wells No. 1 and No. 2 would be retained as standby water sources, for an overall total of five water sources.

The project includes new pipelines, including service laterals and appurtenances (235,000 linear feet), storage tanks, booster pump stations, upgraded wells, treatment systems, and water service connections to eight new residential connections. Older infrastructure and unsafe private wells would either be removed or converted for non-potable irrigation use. The project is intended to improve drinking water quality, increase reliability, and reduce long-term risks from contamination and flooding. The overall project would be constructed in two Phases. The project will use funding from the State Water Resources Control Board (SWRCB) Expedited Drinking Water Grant for Phase I, and from the California Safe Drinking Water State Revolving Fund through the SWRCB for Phase II. The project is located along San Juan Road, Salinas Road, Highway 1, Hilltop Road, Jensen Road, Bluff Road, Trafton Road, and Struve Road within the Coastal Zone and Inland Zone of North County. 

Site Improvements and New Facilities. 
The project involves a Coastal Development Permit and Use Permit for the construction of public utilities and related infrastructure, including approximately 235,000 linear feet of pipeline, including service laterals and appurtenances. The following project components will be implemented as part of the Pajaro Sunny Mesa Springfield Area Regional Consolidation Project: 

PWS Iron and Manganese Treatment System & Facility Flood Protection: The project proposes the installation of a 14-foot-tall 10,000-gallon tank and treatment system to remove high levels of iron and manganese from the existing Pajaro Well No. 1, located at 136 San Juan Road (Assessor’s Parcel Number (APN) 117-351-032-000). The parcel is zoned Public Quasi-Public or “PQP” and is within the inland area of North County, which is guided by the NCAP. The underlying zoning district allows public utility uses and accessory structures, subject to the granting of a Use Permit. Treatment of this well would provide the consolidated water system with an additional and reliable source of potable water. Sludge generated by the proposed Iron and Manganese Treatment System would be discharged to the existing sewer line located within the public right-of-way of San Juan Road. Additional modifications to the site include demolition of existing piping, fencing, and a light pole, and construction of a new 9-foot-tall 1,808 square foot structure for chemical and electrical equipment, an access ramp, retaining walls, and approximately 2,000 square feet of new impervious surfaces at the southeastern corner of the site. The new facilities at this site will be constructed above flood elevation level, and new drainage management features will be installed to manage on-site flood flows. All other equipment, including the existing hydropneumatic tank, would be protected in place. See Exhibit J.

PWS Tank Rehabilitation: The project would include modifications to the existing Pajaro tank and booster pump station located off Railroad Avenue in Pajaro (APNs 117-263-002-000, 117-263-005-000, and 117-263-006-000). The parcels are zoned Public Quasi-Public or “PQP” within the inland area of North County, which is guided by the NCAP. The underlying zoning district allows public utility uses and accessory structures, subject to the granting of a Use Permit. Alterations to the site would support installation of a bypass valve vault, the replacement of the existing 10-inch electromagnetic flow meter, and the rehabilitation of the existing 600,000-gallon welded steel water tank. All proposed improvements will be made within the existing developed site. See Exhibit J.

SMWS Tank Site Upgrades: The SMWS tank site is located off Stone Ridge Drive in Royal Oaks (APN 117-191-004-000). The parcel is zoned Resource Conservation with a maximum gross density of one unit per 10 acres with a Visual Sensitivity overlay or “RC/10­VS” within the inland area of North County, which is guided by the NCAP. The underlying zoning district allows improvements to water system facilities, including wells and storage tanks serving fifteen (15) or more service connections, subject to the granting of a Use Permit. Improvements to the existing tank site include instrumentation, controls, and communication system improvements to integrate site operation into the proposed centralized Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system. These improvements would also occur entirely within the developed site and would not result in impacts on visual resources given the existing fence screening around the tank site. See Exhibit J.
Transmission Booster Pump Station: The project proposes construction of a new transmission booster pump station located off Elkhorn Road at the existing SMWS well site (APN 117-121-003-000). The parcel is zoned Agricultural Conservation in the Coastal Zone or “AC(CZ),” which is guided by the NCLUP. The underlying zoning district allows public utilities and infrastructure subject to the granting of a Coastal Development Permit. The new station would transport water from PWS to SMWS, then pump water to the Bluff/Jensen Road area and down to the SWS. This system upgrade would provide a total pumping capacity rate of 700 gallons per minute (gpm). Other project components include a bypass vault, on-site security improvements, relocation of the existing water meter and lateral for the adjacent property to the north, replacement of the existing driveway access, and installation of approximately 150 square feet of new impervious surfaces and 2,350 square feet of replacement impervious surfaces. This site would retain the existing SMWS Wells No. 1 and No. 2 to serve as standby water sources. This portion would require the removal of two Coast Live Oak trees. See Exhibit J.

Bluff/Jensen Tank and Pump Station Site: The project proposes the construction of a new booster pump station and water storage tank on a 10,000 square foot portion of an approximately 461,736 square foot (10.6 acre) site at the corner of Bluff and Jensen Road (APN 117-033-005-000). The parcel is zoned Agricultural Conservation in the Coastal Zone or “AC(CZ),” which is guided by the NCLUP. The underlying zoning district allows public utilities and infrastructure subject to the granting of a Coastal Development Permit. This system component would transport water from the transmission main into the Bluff/Jensen area while providing water flow for fire prevention. The pumping facility consists of a 24-foot-tall 125,000-gallon potable water storage tank, four vertical turbine can pumps, a hydropneumatic pressure tank, a back-up generator, and construction of a 229 square foot chemical and electrical building housing a tank mixing and chlorine residual control system. Site access would be provided by a new 20-foot-wide driveway with a rolling gate on Jensen Road. Other site improvements include 8-foot-tall security fencing and a transformer. The Bluff/Jensen tank and pump station would result in the permanent conversion of approximately 0.4 acres of farmland to non-agricultural use. See Exhibit J.

The project involves consolidation and improvements to three water systems operated by the PSMCSD. The District is regulated by the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) and operates multiple water service systems in northern Monterey County. The Project involves consolidating PWS, SMWS, and SWS into one regional system in portions of the North County Area Plan and North County Land Use Plan area. The project components would be located on multiple parcels with zoning designations that include Farmland with a minimum building site of 40 acres (F/40), Resource Conservation with a maximum gross density of one unit per 10 acres with a Visual Sensitivity overlay (RC/10­VS), Public/Quasi Public (PQP), Agricultural Conservation in the Coastal Zone (AC (CZ)), Coastal Agricultural Preserve in the Coastal Zone (CAP (CZ)), and Coastal General Commercial in the Coastal Zone or (CGC (CZ). See Exhibit H.

The project is PQP in nature, and the majority of the project will occur at existing PSMCSD facilities and within existing rights-of-way. The above-listed zoning districts all allow for PQP uses, such as public utility improvements. Public utility uses, accessory structures, and PQP uses are allowed uses, subject to the granting of a Use Permit for the inland areas of North County pursuant to Title 21, and a Coastal Development Permit within the coastal areas pursuant to Title 20. Therefore, the proposed development is an allowed use. The project involves development within 100 feet of ESHA, 750 feet of known archaeological resources, on slopes in excess of 30%, and the removal of two native trees, and therefore requires the granting of Coastal Development Permits in each case. Portions of the project not already connected to the PSMCSD are within the service area according to the maps published by the Local Agency Formation Commission for Monterey County (LAFCO) and will require annexation.

CEQA
PSMCSD prepared an Initial Study Mitigated Negative Declaration (IS/MND) for the project. Potential impacts to biological resources, cultural resources, hazards and hazardous materials, hydrology and water quality, noise, tribal cultural resources, and utilities and service systems were identified, but mitigation measures were applied that reduce the potential impacts to a less than significant level. These mitigation measures are incorporated as conditions of approval for the project. The Initial Study found that there were no impacts or less than significant impacts to all other resource topics. PSMCSD considered comments received during the public review period and they did not alter the conclusions in the IS/MND. Responses and minor revisions to the Initial Study were prepared prior to the adoption of the Mitigated Negative Declaration by the PSMCSD Board of Directors on February 26, 2026. See Exhibit E.

A Mitigated Negative Declaration for the Pajaro Sunny Mesa Springfield Area Regional Consolidation Project (State Clearinghouse No. 2025110647), as revised in response to comments, was adopted by the Board of Directors of the Pajaro Sunny Mesa Community Services District (Resolution No. 02-02-26) on February 26, 2026. 

The proposed project scope was considered in the State Clearinghouse No. 2025110647. No changes in project scope, circumstances, or new information have occurred. Therefore, no additional environmental review is required pursuant to CEQA guidelines section 15162.

All project changes required to avoid significant effects on the environment have been incorporated into the project and/or were adopted by PSMCSD as Mitigation Measures in a Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Plan (see Exhibit F). PSMCSD, as Lead Agency, will be responsible for implementing this plan. As a Responsible Agency for permitting, the County has conditioned the project to require that PSMCSD provide evidence that those measures that are needed to demonstrate compliance with County Code are implemented and have the intended effect (Condition No. 5).

AGRICULTURAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE (AAC) REVIEW: 
The project was referred to the Agricultural Advisory Committee on May 28, 2026. The committee voted to recommend approval of the project as proposed by a vote of 9-0, with 3 members absent. See Exhibit D.

LAND USE ADVISORY COMMITTEE (LUAC) REVIEW: The project was referred to the North County Land Use Advisory Committee (LUAC) on May 6, 2026.  The committee recommended approval of the project by a vote of 5-1, with 3 members absent. One LUAC member expressed concerns regarding the amount of grading in the proximity of sensitive habitat and archaeological resources, which they felt were not completely studied or reviewed. Staff responded to these concerns at the LUAC by confirming that the project applicant prepared and circulated an Initial Study Mitigated Negative Declaration, which thoroughly analyzed potential impacts on these resources. Project impacts have been reduced to a less-than-significant level through the implementation of mitigation measures. See Exhibit C.

RECOMMENDATION:
It is recommended that the Board of Supervisors:
a.  Approve a Standard Agreement (SA) between the County of Monterey (County) and Andrew Thomson, dba Tough Automation to provide programming, maintenance, monitoring, and on-call repair services for the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) network for an initial term of three years effective October 15, 2026 to October 14, 2029, with the option to extend the term for two additional one-year periods, for an amount not to exceed $2,000,000; and
b.  Authorize the Director of Public Works, Facilities and Parks or designee to execute the SA and future amendments to the SA where the amendments do not significantly alter the scope of work or increase the amount by more than 10% ($200,000) of the original approved SA amount of $2,000,000 bringing the potential overall aggregate not to exceed amount to $2,200,000 subject to review and approval as to form by the Office of the County Counsel and as to fiscal provisions by the Auditor-Controller’s Office. 
 
SUMMARY: 
The recommended actions would allow for the approval of a Standard Agreement (SA) between the County and Andrew Thomson, dba Tough Automation (Tough Automation) (Attachment A) in the amount of $2,000,000 to provide maintenance, monitoring, on-call repair, and wireless services for the existing SCADA network and coordinate with the County to expand the SCADA system. 
 
DISCUSSION:
The Department of Public Works, Facilities and Parks (PWFP) relies on the use of the SCADA network to monitor and manage submersible pumps, flow meters, emergency backup generators, alarm dialers, a domestic water well pump, a domestic water storage tank, booster pumps, a fire pump and motor, and to receive and acknowledge alarms for the Pajaro County Sanitation District (PCSD) Wastewater Collection System, the Boronda County Sanitation District - Zone 2 San Jerardo Water System, and the CSA-50 stormwater detention pond pumps. SCADA is a critical centralized system that integrates hardware, software, and communication networks to provide centralized supervision, control, and data analysis.  
 
The County intends to expand the SCADA system to include the Boronda County Sanitation District (BCSD) Wastewater Collection System and the County Service Area 75 - Chualar Wastewater Collection System. Expansion may include other locations as appropriate to enhance operational efficiency and safety. Due to the remote location of the equipment, expertise in off-grid solar powered systems and wireless communications, SCADA systems are essential for the proposed expansion projects.  
 
Tough Automation has more than ten years of experience specializing in wastewater collection lift station controls, domestic water booster pump station controls, wastewater treatment plant control systems, industrial networking, industrial technology, off-grid solar power systems for remote locations, and motor control troubleshooting. Tough Automation has expertise in radio telemetry communication and regularly performs radio studies for identifying adequate communication equipment for remote sites. 
 
Tough Automation previously repaired and restored components of the existing SCADA system including writing new code logic for enhanced functionality. PWFP has researched other service providers and there are other vendors that provide similar services; however, other vendors do not offer all required services within a single company. A County Sole Source Justification for the proposed SA with Tough Automation was recently approved due to their familiarity with the existing SCADA system and the breadth of services that they provide. 
 
Board of Supervisors (Board) approval would allow for the issuance of the proposed SA between the County and Tough Automation to provide maintenance, monitoring, on-call repair, and wireless services for the existing SCADA network and coordinate with the County to expand the SCADA system. The proposed SA has an initial term of three years effective October 15, 2026 to October 14, 2029, with the option to extend the term for two additional one-year periods, for an amount not to exceed $2,000,000.
 
OTHER AGENCY INVOLVEMENT/COMMITTEE ACTIONS:
The Office of the County Counsel-Risk Management, County Information Technology Department and the Auditor-Controller’s Office have reviewed and approved the SA as to form, risk, and fiscal provisions, respectively.  
 
FINANCING:
Sufficient funding is available in the Fiscal Year 2026-27 Adopted Budget for planned services in the amount of $40,000 as follows:
PCSD: Fund 1521, Dept. 320062, Appr. PFP160 = $30,000
BCSD: Fund 1524, Dept. 320064, Appr. PFP162 = $5,000
CSA-75: Fund 1443, Dept. 320060, Appr. PFP158 = $5,000
 
Future funding for these services will be allocated in each future Fiscal Year Budget.
 
BOARD OF SUPERVISORS STRATEGIC PLAN GOALS:
The recommended action aligns with the Board’s Strategic Plan Goals for Safe and Resilient Communities and Well-Being and Quality of Life.  The SCADA network is essential to monitor existing water systems, and the proposed SA will allow the County to optimize the existing system to minimize downtime through proper design and maintenance.
